utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps I can show you something from the NIOD report. It would be page 5 of chapter 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'll give it a D number, an exhibit number, 210 for identification. If we could just put page 5, it will be 5 of 7. It's part 3, chapter 5, section 8, marked as Exhibit D210 for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at I believe it's one, two, three, four. It says: "Karremans ended his report by stating that he had repeatedly warned the commander of the 28th Division that actions outside the enclave borders would provoke reactions from the VRS and possibly put the population in danger. If the ABiH had indeed undertaken actions outside the enclave, then it would mean, as Karremans wrote, that the VRS had restrained itself. The only response was from the usual post with the usual weapons. The VRS could have inflicted great damage if that had been ordered." From here, sir, Mr. Karremans, it would appear that you were rather concrete and not speculative. Would you not agree with me, or is it your opinion that the NIOD report is untrustworthy?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I am being concrete and what is written there is written. But you should not ask speculative questions. Ask me for facts and figures and I will give them to you. Provocation, yes; I mentioned that and I mentioned that in my reports as well, only based on that which observation posts observed, not on what I observed myself because I never once left the enclave. It is logical that when you find that something happens and people leave the enclave, that you discuss that with the leadership of the ABiH and that you point out to them that this might have consequences, particularly toward the population. That is not speculative; that is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it's a fact that you had warned the 28th Division, that is the Muslim army, that they were engaged in provocative acts by going out and carrying out military activities.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Noted by observations from observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But those observation posts, Mr. Karremans, were not foreign observation posts. Right? They were DutchBat observation posts. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And those were your men, trained to provide you with information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it you trusted the information you were receiving.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And having trusted that information, I take it, you then confronted the commander of the 28th Division as a result of what you had been hearing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: That's correct, in the sense that information is always checked. So you don't depend on a single information source; you try to base yourself on several sources. And if those converge and you get a clear picture, then that may be a reason for making such a remark and to inform the leadership of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, what was their response?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: In most cases, none. Either it is correct and we are looking for food, period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I guess I'm not quite clear, because I want to go back to what -- earlier when Mr. Ramiz told you there were no weapons on the helicopter you seemed to believe him. You didn't do any checking - not that there was a way you could check - but you believed what you heard. I'm asking you now when you confronted the 28th Division, did they admit, at least to you, that they were going out and committing atrocities or provoking the Serbs? Did they come clean? Or did they deny this action, in which case they would be giving you false information?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No, they did not deny leaving the enclave, especially during the beginning. There was a route between Srebrenica and Zepa which was frequently used, so we knew that. At a later stage, this changed. You are again mentioning provocations and atrocities, but we have not witnessed those. The fact that in a demilitarised zone, a safer area during the night, people go out, and warning them for this is sufficient to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever give the Muslim army any food from the humanitarian aid that was coming in?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, not you personally, but DutchBat III?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. The food that came in through the UNHCR was for the population and not for the ABiH. How they handled it is something you should ask someone from the ABiH, what they held back for themselves and how the incoming food was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you're saying as far as you know you never allowed any food to be given to the ABiH, the army itself.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: One of our duties was humanitarian support for the population. If at any time an UNHCR convoy came in, then it was the representative of the UNHCR who did business with the local population concerning the distribution of the food and not the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you another map at this point in time, and we'll get back to all of these questions. I want to show you a map. This has been marked for identification purposes -- it's actually -- has come in as evidence, P369. Have you ever seen this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise part of the area, but the borders are entirely different and probably the intentions are probably different as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure we go from the general to the specific. Would you say that in this map the enclave would be found somewhere or be contained?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: It's not on the map, but it could be drawn on to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm trying to get at. Would the enclave be in this -- on this -- you know, on this map? Could it be contained in it?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, perhaps you may want to have the other map handy, the one that we showed you earlier that has the enclave, if you want to have that for a reference. And I would like you to please draw on this particular map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Since this is our copy, we will have to give it an exhibit number as D211 for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like you to draw on it the enclave, the enclave as it existed pursuant to the UN resolutions and as you had found it when you got there, if you could.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a reason why, sir?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be too time-consuming to draw the exact border on this map that I'm not familiar with, given that I'm aware of the dispute during the period of DutchBat I, DutchBat II, and DutchBat III where both parties tried to talk about enclave borders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: At this point, in my view, it would be too time-consuming to indicate an exact enclave border. There are better maps, military maps, than this one where it is indicated precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, first of all let me inform you that we're not really disputing where the borders are between I, II, and III DutchBat, that's not an issue. It doesn't have to be totally precise. Then we can take an early break and you can have 30 minutes. But just in general, and the purpose is for other reasons. So it would be just in general so you could trace it so we could see at least within this geographical region that is marked out where the enclave would be located.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Well, it's possible but there's no point at this time because there's no difference in interpretation between DutchBat I, II, and III; it's the difference in the dispute between the two parties. So borders differ and have changed over a certain period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you may put a question to this witness to see whether the safe area is within the dark part of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was going to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're on the same wavelength on this one, Your Honour. I have to get there, but I'm there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in this -- if you look at this map, the one that I presented you that on the screen, you will see that there is a marked-up area. Could you please tell us whether the enclave itself is included within this bordered area on the map.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No, I can't, because then I would need to follow the entire enclave border - that would take time - I would need to do that from one place to another, one road to another. I drove around there for six months and I know what the area looked like. I can't do that with this map. I can't transform this map into a much better map. And once again, I'm not sure where you're headed here, but there are very specific maps that indicate the borders agreed at the time and that were subject to dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me help you out here. Let me help you out here. The Prosecution's contention is - if I may speak for them, and I often do in this case, much to their dismay - but it's their contention that this area that you see on this map, the one that's on the projector, was the "zone of responsibility" of the Bratunac Brigade during the very same period that DutchBat I, II, III were there. And -- so that's why I'm asking you. So you could show us where the enclave would fit into this "zone of responsibility," as the Prosecution claims existed at the time that you were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the best way is let the Prosecution state what is their position. Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, the other point is to lay a foundation first, asking him: Do you know what the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade was. And then he can -- if yes, he can compare it to this map. And if no, game over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I will take part of the suggestion. I don't believe a foundation is necessary, but I can ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Assuming, assuming, sir, that what is marked on this map that you see on the screen was a zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, would it not appear on the map that part of its zone of responsibility included the very same zone of enclave which you were responsible for?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, not possible. Look at the map. Look at where -- the location.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I don't know where you're headed, and I don't want to make the remark that I made. But I have a diploma in map reading; that was part of my occupation. So if you tell me to draw that into that, then I don't do that. I observe specific borders. And of course we'll find a piece that doesn't quite fit in and a piece that doesn't -- that does fit in, and that is what the dispute is about. No. I'll meet you halfway by taking a good long look at it and drawing it in piece by piece, but not just off the bat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I'll take that. I'll take you up on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we can have an early break, Your Honour, and perhaps the gentleman could look at it and assist. I don't think it should take too long. Now we have Mr. McCloskey up. I take it this is going to be a procedural issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll hear what Mr. McCloskey would like to say. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to try to help and given that the Prosecution's position on all this has been requested. I can just clarify. The Prosecution's position is fundamentally that Potocari on 12 July is within the Bratunac Brigade zone of responsibility, as is Bratunac, as is Kravica, as are the key areas. This is the focus of the Prosecution's position. So -- and we do support Mr. Butler's testimony regarding this map and other issues. But this is, if that will help focus the questions, this is the key position of the Prosecution in this matter. This map and all the attention that's being paid to it, I think the Prosecution's position is getting a little bit warped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I could make the Prosecution's argument for them. I won't, but I can, perhaps not as passionately as they would. But Mr. Butler would have us believe and has been validated at this time that they support that contention, that back in July 1995 the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade encompassed that -- all of that area. And of course assuming that a brigade had a zone of responsibility - a contention which we don't agree with - but assuming that that is the case, their argument is furthered that he would have had control over that area and he would be subject to or be responsible for any activities, including atrocities, occurring within that area. And what I'm trying to demonstrate here is that at the same time Mr. Butler claims that the Bratunac Brigade has a zone -- this geographical zone of responsibility, it would appear - and you don't need to have a degree in map reading or map making - that the enclave is smack right in the middle of this geographical region which they claim is a zone of responsibility. And that is the contention. And then from there I'm going to ask Mr. Karremans - and I'm hoping he will help me out on this one - whether he and Colonel Blagojevic shared the same area of responsibility at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you should put this question directly to this witness. As for the background and the positions of both parties, we believe that we heard a lot of evidence. Well, we'll have our break, and during the break I hope the witness could have a closer look at this map. In the meantime, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you could be thinking well of your questions and line of your questions and have it well organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I take you -- we are streamlining as we are going along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We come to the subject matter step by step. Now we are at the door of it. We are at the door of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have to eat a lot of salad before we get to the main course, but we're there, we're there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sometimes we don't need salad. But we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before we resume, could I make some clarification on your position in this very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And you know, during the proceedings you set July 11th, 1995, as kind of a landmark day in this case. So is it your position that you hold even after the fall of Srebrenica, the enclave, Srebrenica enclave, is still the zone of responsibility of United Nations peacekeepers? Or it falls within the zone of responsibility of the Serb armies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if I may, Your Honour, and with the utmost respect, I don't believe those are the -- that's the universe of choices. But -- and so I can't answer directly. I can state first and foremost at no point in time, at no point in time, that map represented a zone of responsibility or the zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade, because the brigade never had a zone, number one. Number two, we believe that once Srebrenica fell and the enclave was no longer an enclave for an intents and purposes, the line of defence of the Bratunac Brigade changed and continued to change as the days progressed with the searching orders. And then at some point, the Bratunac Brigade went to Zepa and then to Trnovo, so there was no -- there was nothing there in Bratunac as far as we are concerned. So I don't know if I have answered your question, but we want to be clear about that. We believe at all points in time that under the rules the brigade had a line of defence which had a certain length; it went so far forward and so far backwards and that's it. Not a geographical region. Which is exactly why I want the gentleman, Mr. Karremans, to basically give us - in general, for illustrative purposes, not for historical accuracy, so there's no need for you to be concerned that later on someone will come and say "This is what he said" - but for illustrative purposes, to demonstrate that here we have some overlap. Am I making myself clear, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think so far so good. You may proceed with your questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And I take it I have indeed answered your questions to the extent possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Karremans, during the break -- and I apologise for taking up your break when you should be relaxing. But I would suspect someone with your background shouldn't have too much difficulty in looking at the map for illustrative purposes to denote for us the enclave. Did you have an opportunity to do that, sir? Thank you. For the record, Mr. Karremans was shaking his head. If we could go to that. And again we're referring to Exhibit D212. If we could look at that. All right. And could you please explain this to us, Mr. Karremans. Well --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] All right. Based on -- [Interpretation] Based on this map, I traced the positions of the observation posts, the most obvious sites on the map that were always indicated in that reports, for example, Brkok [phoen] and the like, roads that we use. And eventually I put these dots on the map. These dots are approximately the line of and the area of responsibility of DutchBat during the period that I was there. This line indicates that in the northern part the Charlie Company was responsible and in the southern part the Bravo Company was responsible. This is Srebrenica. This is Potocari, where the headquarters were. And you'll see that part of the area of the responsibility of the battalion is outside the purported area of responsibility - with which I'm not familiar; this is the first time I'm hearing about it - of the brigade. So it doesn't overlap. It's larger or differently situated than the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in the transcript I think the witness said that the town of Potocari, but I didn't see it on the transcript. Witness, would you please mark the place called Potocari on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, Your Honour. It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could put a P there, sir, so we could --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There you go. And I take it P is within the enclave.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just for the record C is for Charlie Company and B is for Bravo Company, right.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the area that you have indicated was the enclave, who was responsible for that area during the period that DutchBat III were there?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: The dotted area was the area responsibility of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The DutchBat battalion?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I take it if that was your area of responsibility, the VRS could not operate in that area.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: The VRS or ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The VRS, the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So in other words -- go ahead. You want to finish.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: They had no access to the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's -- I was going to get to that, you know, because I'm just troubled a little bit. So if you can help me out. And these are not trick questions; these are for some nuances in this trial. Could the VRS come in and command and control what was happening in this area? I know you were supposed to and there were some areas that you didn't have access to. But could the VRS come in and command and control at least the portion that is outlined as this zone of responsibility, a term which I dislike immensely?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes, that was possible, just the same as the AB had the opportunity to go outside at night. There were also opportunities to enter at night. Why? Because the enclave border is 50 kilometres long and there were rather few observation posts. And considering the terrain and the elevations and recesses, it was possible to leave and re-enter the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps I inartfully phrased my question. Did the Bratunac Brigade commander have command and control over what was happening inside that portion of the enclave which you at the same time had command and control over by virtue of the UN resolution, the mandate, given to you?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No, they couldn't control it. But you need to formulate the question more clearly, whether they could enter the area under certain conditions, yes or no, and then I would say yes. Control. The battalion was there. But outside because the battalion wasn't there, I had no oversight of that, I had no view of that, so I don't know what happened there. But within the area, there were a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, maybe I'm not phrasing it right. Let me try it this way. Outside the area, the enclave, did you have command and control of what was happening outside that area?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. That doesn't mean that DutchBat soldiers could not go out at night - I'm not saying they did - but they could have gone at night, as we know that the Muslim army was going out wreaking havoc; right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes, but for DutchBat to go outside, that was -- that would exceed the mandate, so in other words it wasn't authorised and we did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm not talking about authorisation. I just want to make sure that we're clear that in the enclave you had command and control and not the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can object if you want. I heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, before that if we can have a time and a date so it becomes more clear, about the area we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm glad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Also an observation. We are comparing apples and oranges if we are talking about an international peacekeeping force on the one side and a local brigade on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the gentleman is perfectly clear to clarify that on cross. I just want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no. I think the first issue is relevant, that is here, are you sure that we are talking about the situation before 11 of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That part I agree, but the apples and oranges, that portion I didn't agree with. I will rephrase or narrow it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the situation is clear. The problem is just a time frame. Put a time frame there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As long as the enclave existed, okay, pursuant to the UN resolution, would it be fair to say that within the borders of the enclave you were supposed to have command and control?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And are you aware that in that resolution, are you aware of any exceptions, deviations, call it whatever you may, that allowed the Bratunac Brigade to share part of the enclave with you so they could -- you could share with them the command and control of that area?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I don't know the area of responsibility of either of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, we're not talking -- I'm just talking about your little, you know, enclave, that area. And if I may use a phrase, I mean from Mr. Ruez, he had indicated that the commander is the master of life and death in an enclave -- in his zone of responsibility. I don't want to go that far. But would it be fair to say that within the enclave, this geographical region, for all intents and purposes you were supposed to have command and control and not share it with either the Muslim army that was supposed to be demilitarised or - and especially - any portions of the Serb army that was located in the area, be it the Milici Brigade, the Bratunac Brigade, the Zvornik Brigade, anyone. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No, that's comparing apples and oranges. I was clearly assigned responsibility for what I indicated by dots. And the peace agreement stipulates that both parties agreed that a certain section of this entire area would be a safe area where neither party would do anything. We discussed that extensively at the beginning. Demilitarisation was also a subject of the discussions. But the area of responsibility and who does what, it was the area of responsibility of DutchBat and not of the ABiH or a VRS brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I think we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think we have a meeting of the minds, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This question has been asked and answered for three times. It's crystal clear. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree. I believe that was very succinct, Your Honour. I was going to complement the gentleman for his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if I can go to another area. I want to speak a little bit about the activities that were known to the VRS during the period while you were the commander of DutchBat. Are you aware of any intelligence with respect to a spring offensive by the Muslim forces against the Serb forces in that area? Were you privy to any information during that period?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No, not that I remember. The spring offensive does not ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We talked a bit about the provocations or the acts of provocations and I think we agree that at some point you came to realise that the Muslim forces were or the Muslim army inside the enclave were going out and perhaps provoking, at least that's what it would appear from reading the NIOD report, which I think is based on a whole lot of interviews, including interviews from you. So you were aware of provocations, but you're saying that you were not aware of any military offensives that were being geared up by the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I didn't say that there were provocations; I said that going outside at night on the part of several Muslim men at a time could have a provocative effect. I said that it -- I didn't say they were provocations but they might have a provocative effect. I don't know what they did. I gave an answer earlier and my answer was that they were looking for food. That is a possible explanation. I didn't hear any other explanations. All I said was it's provoking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And we're going to get to that at some point, but you would agree with me: Killing innocent Serbs and burning down their houses is not the right way to go about looking for food. You would agree with me on that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I can't prove that because I wasn't there and I didn't observe it myself. So this is a remark on your part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't say that. You said they were looking for food, and I'm saying that when you behead somebody or you kill somebody and you burn down their house or their village, that's not exactly an act of looking for food. It's not the same as breaking into a bakery to get a loaf of bread; right? You would agree with me on that.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: It doesn't sound that way, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Again, I want to get back to my earlier question. Were you privy to any intelligence, be it from the UN military observers, your own folks, Sarajevo, Zagreb, New York, anyone, concerning a potential military buildup by Muslim forces for a spring offensive or some sort of an offensive against the Serb forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Not that I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to show you some documents that have already come in so at least we have a point of reference. And I'm going to show you documents. I'll start one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll give the usher all three and he can put them on the ELMO one by one. D194, 195, and 196. We'll start with 194. If you could put it on -- the first page so at least everyone can see. This is a document that came in from the head of intelligence of the Main Staff of the VRS who testified in this court in open, Mr. Salapura. And this document is dated 8 February 1995. This is information to the Main Staff. And if we go to page 2 -- You may wish to stand up there for a little bit. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Page 2. I'm going to read a portion of it. At the last paragraph it says: "Information is confirmed that in Srebrenica enclave, as part of the MV, the Muslim army, general preparation for the spring offensive, Muslim units are being reorganised and trained in order to carry out offensive operations to merge with the 2nd Corps forces on the Drinjaca/Konjevic Polje/Cerska line, thereby intending to establish a territorial link between Srebrenica and the Tuzla region." It then goes on to say: "In connection with that, information is confirmed that five brigades and one sabotage battalion have been formed in Srebrenica. The brigades are of company establishment, 400 to 800 men strong. The most numerous one is the 281 Brigade with a command post in the village of Suceska and the commander is Zulfo Dursumovic," there may be a misspelling of that name, "information is confirmed that the recent contingent that was brought to Zepa by helicopter included a large number of nitroglycerine rifles, a number of mortars, 500 to 800 uniforms and a great quality of infantry ammunition." The date, of course, going back again, is February 1995. And you will agree with me that this is the date when your DutchBat III under your command is in that enclave.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when Mr. Salapura was here, just so you know, I asked him if he was providing false information or misinformation to his superiors, you know. And he sort of chuckled because he thought that would be oxymoronic, for the intelligence officer to be sending his superiors propaganda. So my question is: Were you aware of any of this at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't have the interpretation here. Witness, would you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] My answer was no. [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let me go through a couple of more and I'll double back. There is another document dated 18 May 1995. It came in as a Defence Exhibit 195. If you just put the front page, first page, so we have a reference on that. This is -- again, came in through Mr. Salapura. We see intelligence information and the date, 18 May 1995. If we were to go to page 3. And I will lead again. Paragraph 3, it talks about: "Muslim propaganda is emphasising alleged VRS operations towards enclaves in the Podrinje region. They have started occupying UNPROFOR checkpoints in the Srebrenica area. While in the Gorazde area, on the Gorazde-Ilovaca road, they are using UNPROFOR vehicles to manoeuvre forces and transport materiel and technical equipment, which all indicates that they were preparing offensive operations from the enclaves." So here it would appear that the head of intelligence is telling his superiors that Muslim forces are posing as members of DutchBat or UNPROFOR and they're using UNPROFOR vehicles and so on and so forth. My question is: Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] The answer is no. [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go to the next document, D196. Again, this came in from Mr. Salapura, the head of intelligence. This one is dated 10 June 1995. You're ready to go?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good. Now let me show you D196 dated 10 June 1995, again an intelligence report. If you could look at page 2 at the bottom, it says here: "Muslim forces in the Gorazde (81st Division) and Srebrenica (28th Division) enclaves have raised their combat readiness to the highest level and strengthened their forces at the forward line. They are planning to carry out offensive activities in order to insert troops behind your lines and among our ranks." So now this is approximately a month before the fall of Srebrenica. Were you aware of this intelligence report or this information?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: The same is the case as with the previous two paragraphs or sections I saw. They were written by information from the -- about the VRS, and I'm not familiar with the contents. And I'm not familiar with the background to that information and don't know the source of this intelligence. It was written by intelligence services. I'm not aware of the source of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You would agree with me and I believe you had some folks working for you in intelligence, that usually they work through informants, people who provide them with information. Right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm not asking whether you had seen these actual reports. What I am asking, however, is whether you are aware of what is contained in these reports, that is that there seemed to have been a gradual buildup of the forces inside the enclave.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can I ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I don't think we will need this anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can I ask whether you have an opinion as to this information. Do you think it's true or false?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I just answered your question. I can't have an opinion about that because I'm not familiar with the background to this information. I don't know who the sources are and I don't know what this information was based on when it was written up and I'm not going to suggest how the information was obtained. And I prefer not to share an interpretation with you as to whether it's accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So can -- am I to understand that it is your testimony that you were unaware of any buildup, as is being suggested, in the enclaves in these reports?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. There was a buildup, I already said so. Mainly in the month of June we saw a sort of buildup of ABiH, of large groups of armed units, armed people, but not with the suggestion - as I was just told and I just said - to prepare an attack. I hope that you understand me correctly. I would not -- would like to present this suggestion if what it was I can't tell you. Because I don't have an explanation for that. I didn't have an explanation for it at that time from Ramiz who was commander at that time of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, if I could -- do you know a gentleman by the name of General Smith?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who General Smith was.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: In my field, he was commander of UNPROFOR in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have any interaction with UNPROFOR in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. Once during my stay in Bosnia, I went outside - I mean outside the enclave, outside the safe area - for a leave in the Netherlands. And after I returned, I was the last to enter the area. And on my way back, I stopped at Tuzla. After roaming around for a long time, I stopped there. For the first time to my commander, I gave him a number of suggestions, returned, and I never left the area again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I guess again - and I apologise for inartfully phrasing the question - what I meant was: Did DutchBat interact with UNPROFOR in Sarajevo? I know that you had your immediate commander or up the chain of command was in Tuzla, but did you have any interaction, not personal but professional?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. The interaction consisted of communications through the telephone or through the fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether General Smith or UNPROFOR from Sarajevo would communicate with Tuzla so at least they would know what was going on? In other words, if Sarajevo learned information, they would pass it on to Tuzla so Tuzla could pass it on to you, if indeed it involved your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I hope they did. In the normal military hierarchy, it is normal that information goes from the bottom to the top, including analysis of the information goes from the top to the bottom. And that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could now have the assistance of the usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to go to the part of the NIOD report. I'm going to be showing you -- I have the only copies with me, unfortunately. It would be part 3, chapter 1, section 6, pages 3 and 4. If we could do it in sequence, perhaps -- and again, just for the record, these will be numbered as part of D210 for identification purposes. Now, I've underlined that portion so it would help us focus. If we look at it and if we could perhaps get it focused a little bit. It says here under the one paragraph it says: "The ABiH for getting ready for an offensive." And it says: "Akashi concluded he saw numerous indications." And above it we see about the restrictions on sending fuel supplies to UNPROFOR. It says it was not just the Bosnian Serbs, but it would appear it was the Bosnian Muslims also. If we could go to the next page, same chapter. It says here on the one paragraph, this particular page, "General Smith expected that already by the end of March, the ABiH would take the offensive." And I'm wondering whether any information was being forwarded to you that ABiH was getting ready for an offensive that perhaps might concern the VRS, as we noted from what Mr. Salapura had been informing his superiors at the Main Staff level of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] Answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] I don't know. [Interpretation] I don't know. There was an operation upcoming in the area of the capital of Bosnia far away from the location I was. And that information was based on, say, the daily reports, of which I told you which were passed from the bottom down -- from the top down, sorry. In the preparations for actions in the neighbourhood in -- or safe areas to make a bridge between Srebrenica and Zepa, then my answer has to be no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So I just want to make sure I understand. So as far as you were concerned, you had no information about any activities between Zepa and Srebrenica where the Muslim forces were trying to link up?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: It happened at the beginning. I told you. There has been contact between the safe areas, physically also. People went out and people came in only. During the period we were there, this was being made more and more difficult, but there have been contacts at the beginning. People have left the area and have returned and stayed in Tuzla. And also, people have entered the area from Tuzla. But during this period, this was being made more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During this period, were there any complaints by the VRS concerning the conduct of the Muslim army in the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No, not inside but outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, okay. You're right. They were committing the atrocities outside, but then they were hiding inside. You're right. You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the complaints, I take it, were because after they would go out and commit these atrocities, then they could come in for safe harbour under the blue helmet and the blue shield of the UN -- not that that was your intention, but that's what was going on. Right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That was a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was slightly leading --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Not just slightly leading because you put the answer into your question. We have to hear what the witness is telling us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was trying to streamline, but I was caught on that occasion. I will try to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, were there complaints by the Serb army, the VRS, concerning activities that were -- and atrocities committed by the Muslim forces in the enclave -- from the enclave, outside the enclave?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No, not with regard to atrocities. The fact that Muslim fighters left the enclave during the night, that there were exchanges of fire that we could hear from the observation posts and complaints regarding the fact that Muslim fighters stayed in the neighbourhood of an UN observation post and from those positions fired at VRS positions. That is a complaint we also regularly heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the reason they would be firing -- well, let me rephrase it. They would be -- what's the reason why they would locate themselves, position themselves, at a DutchBat observation point and fire from that point on the direction of the Serbs? Why would they do that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I think the answer is clear: To blame someone else, that is, DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course, if the Serbs, Serb forces, were to think that the DutchBat were engaging in those sorts of activities, that is firing at them, what might the Serbs do?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: That's also clear: To fire back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if the Serbs had fired back directly at the DutchBat, what would the DutchBat then do, under the rules of engagement as the UN had provided at the time?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Under the rules of engagement, which were extremely restricted in my view, report that what had happened. It's all very local. It's not big; that came later. But we're talking about small, local activities from both sides. And attempts were made on both sides to find out what the reactions would be. And in a number of cases, DutchBat intervened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- again, I must be a little tired today. If the Serbs were firing at the DutchBat thinking that the DutchBat had been firing at them, you would not just have a chat with the Serbs, you would be contacting your superiors to see, perhaps, whether you needed some intervention. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You wouldn't be asking for any air support?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you aware that in the course of these proceedings we've had testimony where your men have indicated that they were positioning themselves and trying to draw fire from the Serbs in order so you could have a call-in for air power to come in against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just to be fair to the witness - I'm not suggesting Mr. Karnavas isn't - but to put it into a time-frame perspective. Perhaps the witness's response may vary as to when we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I'll lay a foundational question first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did the rules of engagement change at any time while the DutchBat were there?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was close air protection ever available to the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Before the post-air strike guidance somewhere from May 1995 there was. But in the issued post-air strike it was not unless -- and for the remainder, the escape or the way out was always an utmost emergency to utilise that anyway. And that is what happened from July the 6th onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But I just want to make sure we have the ground rules set. Correct me if I'm wrong. As I understand it, DutchBat, not just III but II, was rather small in numbers. And part of the agreement was that there would be air support to assist those small numbers, is that correct, in the eventuality it was needed?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In principle. So I'm going back to where we were before. If the Serbs think that the Dutch are engaged in battle with them, are attacking them, are on the offensive, this peacekeeping mission which is supposed to be there to demilitarise the area and to keep, you know, the status quo, if you may, and if the Serbs engage back sufficiently enough to cause some alarm, are you telling me, sir, that you did not have the option to call in for the planes to come from Italy or wherever, to hit those positions of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. That did not fit into the policy. The UNPROFOR commander and UNPF -- UN protective force commander, Janvier, on the basis of, let me say, a relatively simple attack or an exchange of shots, to apply for air support. Because applying for air support and implementing air support is so incredibly difficult that it -- this is not done simply because fire is being exchanged. But again, on and after July the 6th, things were entirely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we're going to speak about what Janvier's policies were and the reasons why he had those policies. But do you know whether those Muslims forces that were firing at the Serbs in order to give the impression that it was UNPROFOR firing at them, do you know whether those Muslim forces were aware of the complications of you actually getting air strike support? Had you explained that to them?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. For applying for air support under these circumstances was not an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand it wasn't an issue. Because you knew what the circumstances were. But I'm saying -- what I'm asking is: Do you know for a fact whether the Muslim forces that were provoking the Serbs in order to fire upon the Dutch, did they, in fact, know what degree of attack was needed or required before you could call in for close air support? That's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I didn't explain them, but I assume that they were not aware of the post air strike policy unless it was through the ABiH that they had become informed. We also have a completely different idea of the way of operating than the guys in that area. It would take me too far to discuss this at length now, but we tried to explain a number of times how a unit, a DutchBat unit, should function in that area with reference to the utilisation of vehicles and so on. So we don't need to talk about air support at all, because that is far beyond the level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you for a fact, sir, at any point in time take any measures, I mean concrete measures, to apprehend or to stop those who were committing those activities, engaged in those activities?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's difficult in the dark because you can't see them. Secondly, a logical reaction was always to deposit the complaints with Ramiz. And this -- it's the same when the VRS deposited complaints with me during talks after VRS troops have been fired at. And to try to solve it through provocations, that's what I call provocative behaviour to try and stop it, at least to nothing. And at that time there are three parties involved in which DutchBat is located as an independent party between two other parties. I was clear in explaining this type of action towards both sides. And in many cases, this was taken seriously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Only indeed in the latter period, final period, a little less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you think that perhaps of the continuation of this sort of activity and perhaps the impotence of DutchBat to prevent this activity from continuing, that the VRS may have formed an impression that DutchBat or the UN was giving aid and comfort to the Muslim forces inside the enclave?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: That is a question I cannot really answer. At best, I can say perhaps, but no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. No you can't answer it or no --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I can't answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But their complaints were legitimate, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we going until 1.30? 1.45? I wasn't clear on the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you finished that section or if you could not finish your next section in 15 minutes, we could have a break and we could resume at 3.00 and sit until 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. I think a break at this point in time may be good so I can even streamline a little bit more, in keeping with the expectations of the Trial Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we'll have a break and we'll resume at 3.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.29 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we resume, could I ask you a question, Mr. Karnavas. It seems to me that we had a strange menu with a very large appetiser. I believe we had a bite of the main course when we were in our proceedings and then we returned back to the appetiser again. So, Mr. Karnavas, would you please tell me how much this lunch or dinner will last.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's a five-course meal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's a five-course meal. So I wanted to finish up some points and then I would suspect that we're going to be moving right along into some issues. I'm anticipating a lot of the cross, so I'm covering their ground as well. But we're almost there. We're almost there. Delayed gratification is the best gratification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because of the technical problems, this Bench could not sit next Monday and Tuesday, so we have to finish the testimony of this witness. So could you please indicate how many hours do you still need or whether we have an extra, extra sitting tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, we will definitely need an extra sitting, an extra sitting. At the pace that we're going and -- I'm hoping that we can -- I've streamlined somewhat my cross - my direct, I'm sorry. Slip of the tongue there - of the witness. I've streamlined it so I'm hoping that perhaps I can finish as early as after the third sitting tomorrow. There may be a chance of finishing up after the second sitting. But I would hope that once we hit tomorrow, tomorrow morning, I would suspect the first and second sitting will be very quick and will -- but I'm laying the groundwork. Hopefully we will finish with that. I had anticipated in playing portions of the video. Initially I was going to play almost all of the video with all of the meetings, anticipating that the Prosecution would want the videos in their entirety. They're shaking their head. I don't want to appear as though I'm trying to hide something, so I'll narrow that down. It will be streamlined. I was told by the Prosecutor, they may have changed their mind, I believe they said something to the effect of no more than a sitting. So -- but I hope to give them two sittings. So hopefully at the end of the second sitting tomorrow, I'll be through, Your Honour. But don't hold me to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it is really a five-course dinner. And first I want to say that you still have the chance for re-direct. So I wonder whether there's need for you to anticipate the questions that will be put to this witness by the Prosecution. Secondly, I'm not sure there is a necessity for you to play the video because we have seen this video many, many times. There must be a point in playing that video. Maybe you could ask a question first. If this witness could not remember a certain person or a certain conversation, then you played that fragment of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There is -- I could isolate it to maybe a minute or two, very small snippets. I did speak with Mr. Karremans yesterday and asked him if he did see the video recently. I want to be fair to the gentleman and give him an opportunity to -- there are a couple of just minor snippets, but essential to the questions. I think it would be helpful to Mr. Karremans, especially in light of the subject matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But still there's room for improvement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Always. Always. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karremans. Let me pick up where we left, and I'm going to try to move at a fairly rapid clip. We were talking earlier about some of the incidents that might have occurred and what if anything you had become aware of from intelligence reports or otherwise. And I just want to share with you some information. Perhaps you can help us out here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could show the gentleman a portion of the, again the NIOD report. And I'm reading from -- this is part 3, chapter 5, section 8, and this would be on page 2 of 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to sort of the middle of the page. You see above it there's a subtitle which says: "Actions of the warring factions in the period 25 May to 6 July." If we go down and I'll just read the relevant portion. It states: "In mid-June, the ABiH laid an ambush in inhospitable and difficult terrain, 7 kilometres in a straight line outside the enclave border to the south of Zeleni Jadar. A small lorry that was taking VRS soldiers home on leave from the lines around Srebrenica was caught in the ambush. Three soldiers died and nine were wounded." Mr. Karremans, did you hear of this incident?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I don't remember. I'm giving you an honest answer. Of course we heard frequent reports of these irregularities, but as far as an ambush is concerned just outside the enclave, I don't remember much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this was outside the border of the south of Zeleni Jadar. You know where that area is, do you not, Zeleni Jadar? Is my memory correct in serving me that sometime around that period, perhaps thereafter, there was a clash between the VRS and the -- or the VRS advanced to take a portion of the road, cutting --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I'm not sure quite what you mean by the -- advanced VRS. Of course these incidents were commonplace and I don't remember all of them. I don't remember this one, especially because you say people were injured and there were even some casualties. So I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, at one point OP Echo was pushed, was it not? That's the Observation Post Echo. Right around June.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. In early June after I received a warning that I discussed with the battalion staff, OP Echo was attacked. It was not advanced, it was attacked, and it was taken by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that by Zeleni Jadar, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes, around that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And around that neighbourhood it seems where the ambush took place, where Serbs were ambushed by the Muslims and were killed and were wounded. Now, does that refresh your recollection that perhaps that might have been the reason why there was that attack?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. Considering the time frame, that's possible. But we -- in fact, we moved OP Echo back. So the piece that you saw at first, we lost that -- from our perception, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that piece that was lost. Well, let me ask you this: During the period that you were there and perhaps even before you, there was always a dispute, was there not, as to the actual boundaries. You know, the Serbs had their vision of where the boundaries were, the Muslims had theirs, and of course the UN had their own. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that area the -- there was a road that apparently -- where the attack took place, was there not, where the Serbs wanted to control a certain portion of the road?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: But we're assuming the border of Buljim from 1923. That's the base for exactly where the border is. That's why I was talking this morning about the ongoing, interminable dispute between parties about the exact location of the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But that attack that we were speaking about, the one with respect to capturing OP Echo, that was because the VRS wanted to control the -- or to link up with Milici, the part of that road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is leading, but I'm actually pointing him in that direction and asking him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But you may proceed. It is a leading question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's slightly overboard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But here I'll let you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what the objective of the VRS in capturing OP Echo was?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Well, you just indicated that yourself. They wanted a connecting road between the area that they controlled on the side of OP Echo toward the bauxite mines so they could have unhindered access to the road network there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And now if we could go back to the document that we have in front of us. And again for the record that would be for identification purposes as D201 -- 210, I'm sorry. The next paragraph it says: "On 14 June, three soldiers of the VRS Milici Brigade went to pick up berries in the areas outside the minefield." Apparently it was berry season, as we've learned throughout the trial. "They were caught in an ambush in the deserted village of Bozici, to the west of the enclave. Two of the three soldiers died and the third managed to escape. According to the VRS, the bodies of the two who died were mutilated. According to the Drina Corps, five soldiers of the VRS Milici Brigade had already died earlier in the same way." Mr. Karremans, were you aware of this incident? Did you ever learn of it?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there was another incident that got some prominence. Perhaps you can tell us whether you've heard of this one, and this is the incident called Visnjica incident. Did you ever hear of that one?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I don't know what it's about. What was the incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's see if we could perhaps refresh your memory. If I could refer to -- again, to a portion of the NIOD report, for identification purposes, as D210. And now we're looking at part 3, chapter 5, section 8. It's a rather lengthy piece but in light of the time constraints and given that we can read it at our leisure and pluck whatever we need from it for our respective sides, I just want to point you to page 3. I'll just read the first paragraph because I think it's rather interesting. It says -- it starts with: "What became known as the Visnjica incident was an important catalyst for the later events in East Bosnia. This incident, which was given much publicity, was the final and most extensive of the whole series of incidents in and around the enclave before the attack on Srebrenica and is also the one that penetrated the deepest into Bosnian Serb territory." Then it goes on: "Whereas in the years 1992 and 1993, raids from the enclave were mainly intended to acquire food, in 1995 the raids had a mainly military objective which was to tie up the VRS around the enclave. In this way, the ABiH wanted to prevent reinforcements from East Bosnia influencing the conflict in Sarajevo. In addition, the action was intended to influence the morale of the VRS by creating panic and causing a feeling of uncertainty." And if we go on to the next few pages which I won't read, but am tempted, it talks about this particular incident. Do you recall any incident at or about that time where approximately 150 men took part in it, penetrating very deep with Bosnian Serb territory?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. I recall one incident, which we called the tunnel incident, which involved shooting inside the enclave and it's possible that this incident involved the tunnel. When I read this, this sounds like something different where people went outside. And my answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, a tunnel might have been involved in part of the incident, but it says here that this incident received special attention because the New York Times devoted an article to it so it attracted the interest of the UN headquarters in New York and a Security Council briefing had to be given. I guess it perked up their interest. It says that the newspaper wrote that "The incident illustrated UNPROFOR weaknesses because the UN troops had not succeeded in keeping the ABiH within the area that had been demilitarised." Then if we go -- and I'm reading from page 6 incidentally. And then it goes on: "The following day" -- before I go there. Does this ring a bell at all? Does it seem a little familiar to you? Okay.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It goes on: "The following day the International Herald Tribune printed an article and Karremans responded and defended himself in a letter to the Crisis Staff of the army. In his view the article illuminated the situation in and around the enclave in a one-sided way. It would be advisable to spend some time in an enclave before writing about" and then that's the end of the sentence. But I guess my question now is: Mr. Karremans, do you recall writing about this incident which got notoriety?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I do not remember it at this time. Again, I'm referring to something that was a major tunnel incident, but I think you're talking about something entirely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking where -- the tunnel incident was a rather, I believe, unsuccessful mission. And on their way back, it would appear, according to the NIOD report, that the Muslim group opened fire on a part of this village Visnjica and an older woman was hit in the leg. The village itself -- they set fire to five houses, as was confirmed by an ABiH source. So it seemed like -- as if they were probably frustrated that they were not able to succeed in their military mission so they took it out on the houses. And this poor old woman who was going about doing her business, which is why the "New York Times" wrote about it. And I'm wondering whether now this helps you remember the specific incident.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: Yes. That one I do remember with respect to the woman and the weapons that we found the remainders of weapons, the remainders of mortar shells. And if I remember correctly, this took place on June 24th. In the morning we performed an investigation. I inquired at any rate at Ramiz al-Sadric [phoen] and he denied anything. And we never really found out who was responsible. Listening to your version, it sounds like the ABiH might have used its own people, for example, to shoot that old woman and to have set the part of the village or some houses on fire out of frustration. And I know that to this day I have not -- I have no suspicion that they are responsible for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, it's not my version; it was the NIOD report that I was reading from, first of all. I'm not necessarily saying that everything they write is correct, but it is from their report. And so perhaps there may be something to it. But can I ask you: Is it that because Mr. Ramiz informed you or denied having anything to do about it that you believed that they had nothing to do about this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: No. I could not get a clear answer. I couldn't really get my foot in the door regarding the day that it happened. After we conducted the investigation, that we had the investigation conducted by Section 5 of the battalion representative -- the royal military constabulary, I could not ascertain who was responsible for this incident. When people say "we don't know about anything" doesn't necessarily mean that I'll believe that. I've always had doubts as to who was responsible for that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But other than that incident, am I correct in understanding that you didn't hear of any other incidents?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: I don't recall, but I don't believe that I was aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Because when Mr. Franken was here, who I believe he was your chief of staff, and I had the opportunity and privilege to question him - and this can be found on his -- in the transcript, it's on page 1540 - I asked him a question and I said: "You learned of two particular incidents with respect to Muslims going out and committing atrocities upon the Serbs. Is that correct?" And I've just read from line 2, page 1540. And he was questioned on September 15th, 2003. His answer was: "That's correct." So I asked him if this was a form of provocation. That's on line 14, and his answer, again, was "yes." So it would appear that your chief of staff, who is your number two, had learned of these incidents, but you, the commander, was not aware of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't have the Franken testimony here, but if Mr. Karnavas could point out when these incidents occurred, the ones that Franken talks about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There are two incidents I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There are two incidents; it's in his transcript. And I don't -- I'd have to go through the particular dates, but again if you look at my question posed earlier, the foundational question, I asked him other than the one incident. And Mr. Karremans said he hadn't heard. In here there were two incidents referred to by Mr. Franken but I can find that at some point for the record. I just don't want to waste precious time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, but I believe Mr. Karremans said earlier that the incidents were common. So if you now refer him to two specific examples, I think it would be fair just to tell him -- maybe it can be done later. It doesn't need to be done now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I can look through it during the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I certainly don't want to leave the impression that I'm being unfair to the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I asked you earlier another question about BiH soldiers posing themselves as DutchBat or as UN soldiers. And you said that you had no knowledge of that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KARREMANS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And now I want to at least point -- perhaps we can look at the debriefing, which is Prosecution Exhibit 851 for identification. If we could look at page 45, paragraph 4.13. If you could put that on the ELMO. I'll just read. I'll go slowly. It says: "BiH soldiers, complete with blue caps or blue hats, came within a distance of 15 metres from one of the observation posts. Resembling UN personnel, they opened fire from this position in the direction of the BSA front line, so that it seemed as if the UN had opened fire. In this way, they attempted to draw fire from the BSA on the OP" -- observation post -- "and thus involve DutchBat in the combat actions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't posed a question yet, so perhaps he may wish to wait for the question before he gets excited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, earlier you indicated that they -- that Muslim forces or soldiers were firing near the observation post in the direction toward the Serbs. Here it also appears, however, that they were posing themselves as if -- you know, dressed in or resembling UN personnel in blue caps or blue hats. Did you notice that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It appears that this is a specific incident they are talking about, you know, with a distance of 15 metres. Again, it would be fair to point out when this incident occurred so the witness can respond properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm reading from the debriefing report, Your Honour, which the Prosecution has been trying to get in for months now. That's all I have. I'm just asking the gentleman whether he heard of this. He was on the ground. The debriefing is during the period of, I would suspect, DutchBat III, but this is -- and the title is: "Misuse of uniforms." And just to be fair, on point 4.11 it says: "Both BSA and BiH soldiers have worn UN uniforms or at least uniforms bearing a strong resemblance to these." So this is -- and I'm wondering whether he was aware of it, he indicated no. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, you may answer this question first. If there's any problem, Mr. Karnavas, I believe you have to furnish the witness with a specific date later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll try to dig one up from this report. My general question is -- and if he was not there, I would like to know whether he learned that this was going on with DutchBat I or DutchBat II.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to keep the answer brief. During DutchBat I as well as during DutchBat II and III military clothing was stolen, particularly in the part where the soldiers' laundry was done by local staff. So we noted that especially young people in Srebrenica sometimes walked around in army green shirts or wearing blue caps. It says here under item 4.13, though I can hardly believe it, that these people wore specifically a cap over their beret to transmit -- to make an impression to the ABiH. That later happened. I already said that this morning.
